summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex surgical history, including sclerosing mesenteritis and prior gastrocutaneous fistula, was admitted five days after surgical closure due to increasing pain, erythema, and induration at the incision site. She was afebrile and hemodynamically stable. Imaging revealed a superficial fluid collection, and bedside incision and drainage were performed. Cultures grew Escherichia coli and Proteus vulgaris, both sensitive to antibiotics. She was initially treated with vancomycin for MRSA prophylaxis, but antibiotics were discontinued due to clinical improvement and superficial healing by secondary intention. Pain was managed with IV Dilaudid, then transitioned to acetaminophen. She was discharged home with wound care instructions, a visiting nurse, and follow-up planned. No further antibiotics were prescribed.
